label: late original phase / <DEL> in sequences starting with a/q/b that contain o,i,x,2,3
explanation: Sparse feature (0.02% of steps) that fires only at the late original-phase steps (t=3..9, mostly orig_idx 4-7) and the <DEL> step, plus a few recall_idx 1 copy steps. It never fires at t<3 or after the first copy steps. It is strongly enriched for sequences whose first token is a (16.8x lift, 58% of mass), q or b, and for prefixes that contain o, i, x, 2 or 3 (prev_tok i is 10x, prev2_tok o is 9x). The top examples look like a o o 3 i ... and a q o o o c .... The predicate first_tok in {a,q,b} AND at least two of {o,i,x,2,3} seen AND phase<=1 recovers about 70% of activation mass, but precision is only about 2%, and narrower conjunctions raise precision to about 6% at the cost of recall. So the feature reads like a distributed combination of hidden-state memory of these specific tokens, not a clean boolean. Coverage is somewhat better for the higher-activation quartiles, but I did not find a clean magnitude modulator.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=a (+5.92), orig0=q (+4.67), prev_tok=i (+3.98), orig0=b (+3.85), orig2=3 (+3.65), orig1=q (+3.17). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-3.97), phase=2 (-3.35), prev3_tok=q (-2.86), prev3_tok=a (-2.55).
